messages:
Alex Rivera: Heads-up: noticing repeated cross-region failovers from us-east1 -> eu-west1 this morning. App logs show a spike in NAT translations and 502s. CC @Priya @Chen
Priya Kapoor: What's the trigger? LB healthchecks or GeoDNS shifting weights?
Chen Wu: Seems like both. LB probe latency in eu-west jumped ~250ms, our geo-dns auto-weight moved ~70% traffic there. NAT SNAT ports near exhaustion on a few border boxes.
Morgan Lee: Confirming. Cloud NAT metrics show port_util > 0.95 on 3 instances. We're seeing egress errors from GPU nodes that open lots of outbound sockets.
Alex Rivera: We need a mitigation that avoids domino failovers. Proposal: introduce a 'quarantine' warm-up when a region reports errors — keep region in rotation but reduce inbound weight by ~20% and prevent hard pinning. Also set geo-dns TTL to 30s during the incident to allow faster rebalancing. Thoughts?
Priya Kapoor: +1 quarantine. Also add a short backoff for the auto-weight algo: require 3 consecutive probe failures within 60s before shifting >=10% weight. That should prevent oscillation.
Chen Wu: Operational details: change two configs -> 1) route-controller: fallback_policy = quarantine, warmup_percent = 0.8 2) dns: incident_ttl = 30. I'll draft a k8s ConfigMap patch. Need a small canary plan to avoid global churn.
Morgan Lee: Also we should buy time by scaling reserved NAT capacity: route ~15% of egress via reserved nat-pool in us-east-fallback region. Costy short-term but prevents packet drops. Update alert thresholds to port_util > 0.8 so we trigger earlier.
Alex Rivera: Agreed — cost acceptable for a 2h emergency window. Priya can you sign off to spin reserved pool?
Priya Kapoor: Approved. Also implement a shadow probe that keeps long-lived TCP connections open to detect SNAT pool leaks.
Chen Wu: Patch ready. Pushing config diff to gist: https://gist.github.com/fake/patch1. Snippet: ```yaml
fallback_policy: quarantine
warmup_percent: 0.8
shift_threshold:
  consecutive_failures: 3
  window_sec: 60
dns:
  incident_ttl: 30
```
Morgan Lee: Doing the NAT reservation and reroute now. infra-bot, please open an incident ticket and link the runbook.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-489 by Morgan Lee — https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-489 (auto-note: tagged eng-infra, severity: medium)
Alex Rivera: Runbook (condensed): 1) apply route-controller ConfigMap 2) update geo-dns TTL 3) activate reserved NAT pool + reroute 4) monitor port_util, 5xx rate, and LB probe latency 5) keep changes for up to 2h, rollback if 5xx increases or latency spikes further.
Priya Kapoor: Add a synthetic test: `curl -H "X-Test:probe" http://probe.eu-west/longconn` — verify connection reuse and stable latency.
Chen Wu: Deploying to staging -> canary (eu-west small) -> global if canary good. Commit tag c3f5e2. Will push in ~3m.
Morgan Lee: Reserved NAT applied. After reroute port_util dropped to 0.62 on the affected instances within ~90s. 5xxs down ~65%.
Alex Rivera: :thumbsup: excellent. Keep telemetry on for 30m. If we still see oscillation we'll disable auto-weight and enforce static weights for 24h.
Priya Kapoor: I'll track cost delta: estimated cross-region egress + reserved NAT ~ $1.2k for the 2h window. Logging in cost tracker.
Alex Rivera: Thanks team. Once stable I'll write a short post-incident note and the formal runbook addition for 'quarantine' fallback behavior.
Chen Wu: Noted — will include the config snippet and a test plan in the incident doc.
Morgan Lee: Closing loop here, ping if anything regresses.
Alex Rivera: Appreciated.
